chunks: And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
When the time enters, ritual purity and prayer become obligatory, and there is no prayer except with purity.

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: If he prays before the time intentionally, he must repeat it; and if he made a mistake in that and the time caught up with him while he was still in it, it suffices for him; and if he finished it before the time, he must repeat it.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing prayer before its designated time in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Reported from Imam al-Baqir (AS) and cited by Shaykh al-Tusi, this hadith delineates the precise conditions for the validity of prayer based on the entry of its prescribed time. It establishes a critical jurisprudential distinction: intentional early prayer requires repetition, whereas an unintentional error is excused if the time enters during the act, while completing the prayer before the time enters necessitates repetition. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the strict adherence to 'waqt' (time) as a pillar of ritual validity.
